title: Joe Brady Breaks Down Week 2 Victory Over Detroit Lions | Buffalo Bills
headline: DJ Moore's injury is the key watch item: he is day-to-day with a possible one-game absence, while Keon Coleman, Dalton Kincaid, and Deone Walker earned praise after Week 2.
summary: Coach Joe Brady said DJ Moore's injury is not severe but he may miss one game, and the team will see how he recovers over the long weekend since there is no practice until next Wednesday. Ed Oliver was ruled out before the Lions game after a late-breaking pain report during the pregame process, and players were undergoing tests and MRIs on Friday. Brady said Josh Allen had no concerns after reports of him being unwell, calling it typical pre-Thursday-game IV treatment. On the offense, Brady said the team is still defining its identity, that the run game and Allen's aggressiveness on first downs stress defenses, and that the offense left points on the field. He praised Keon Coleman for his six catches, the key third-and-seven conversion, and his trust with Allen while filling in for Moore. Brady praised Dalton Kincaid's blocking and versatility, and said Deone Walker's two batted balls and expanded role showed he is trending up. He also said Keleki Latu's role will keep growing and that Skyler Bell is ready, though he did not name Bell as the next starter. Brady took responsibility for poor clock management on the final two-minute drive before halftime. The team now has ten days to prepare for the Chargers.

title: HC Sean Payton on the Broncos’ home-field advantage: ’We feed off that’
headline: Payton says Jaylen Waddle will get his touches and that the team is working on getting him involved early, while stressing home-field crowd noise as a real advantage for the defense.
summary: Payton said the team's energy and focus were good in both practices this week, with a heavier third-down emphasis and a more extensive red-zone session planned for Saturday. He stressed that defending the home field matters and that crowd noise disrupts the offense's cadence and communication, especially on silent snap counts, and said the team feeds off its fans. On the schedule, he called the short week a deliberate result of the Monday-night setup and said recovery and playing at home are important. He discussed the opponent's quarterback, Lawrence, noting his big arm and ability to escape the pocket and throw on the move. On the offense, Payton said the team wanted to get Jaylen Waddle involved early in the last game, would be more deliberate about it without forcing it, and that he will have his touches. He also talked about the league's cycles of heavier personnel groupings, saying 13-personnel looks force defenses to close edges, and that he still wants a balanced run-pass game on first and second down. Payton also said he is trying to get more sleep and go home earlier, since fatigue can cloud decision-making.

signals.claim: Waddle will get early and continued touches in the offense going forward
signals.note: Payton addressed a deliberate plan to get Waddle involved early after the last game, which points to a more consistent target role.
signals.quote: But you know he's going to have his touches.

topics.detail: Payton said crowd noise makes it harder for the offense to handle the cadence, motions, and communication, and that the team feeds off its home crowd.
Practices have had good energy and focus. Third-down work is the main emphasis, with an extended red-zone session planned for Saturday.

Payton said heavier looks like 13 personnel can reduce the defense's options and help the tackles by making it easier to close edges, while the offense still wants balanced run-pass calls on early downs.
Payton said the rest after a Monday game is a factor in the schedule and that playing at home helps. He also said more efficient late-night work and better sleep are priorities for the staff.
Payton was asked about a punt returner after an injury but gave a limited answer, saying the team has several players who have taken reps there depending on where the punt comes from.

title: Campbell on Week 2 performance
headline: Campbell says Week 2 loss to Buffalo came down to execution and coaching; CB Avonte Maddox left on crutches with no clear status yet.
summary: Campbell credited Buffalo and said the Lions didn't play or coach well enough, taking responsibility himself. He said the offense stalled early and hasn't produced much, and that the run game must become more efficient and consistent. Defensively he cited too many explosive plays, missed fits and coverage busts on the back end, and communication issues in the secondary, especially after the team chose to play more aggressively. He described the run defense as having a mix of players who can pressure and stop the run, and said the front should improve with more time together. He said the pass game picked up in spurts, and that the team has a long way to go on both sides. He was uncertain about Avonte Maddox's status and said he would know more the next day. He said the staff will review the tape, and the team will shift focus to the Jets next.

title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Davante Adams discuss preparation for the Giants, lessons from Week 1 in Australia & more
headline: Myles Garrett is out at least four weeks after surgery, and Kamren Kinchens sat out Thursday's practice with a hamstring injury before the Monday night game vs. the Giants.
summary: McVay opened with the injury report: Kamren Curl (ankle), Omar Speights (hip), and Nathan Landman (shoulder) were limited, Kamren Kinchens (hamstring) did not practice, and Davante Adams took his normal rest day. He said Myles Garrett's surgery went well and he is already walking without crutches, but McVay would not give a firm timeline beyond a minimum of four weeks and said Garrett won't be rushed back. On Aaron Donald, McVay said the key benchmark is how he feels, since he has not had many 11-on-11 reps, and he hopes Donald has good work this week. McVay called the Giants physical, energetic, and well-schemed, with playmakers on all three levels, and said the team needs to match that edge. He downplayed the Week 1 loss in Australia, saying the team should focus on preparation and not dwell on it. Looking at the offense, McVay said the team never got into rhythm, and he praised Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, Kevin Dotson, Alaric Jackson, and Warren McClendon for their run-game work, while stressing that consistency is the goal. He said Stafford's performance was not a major concern and that the QB has handled adversity well. Stafford added that the offense needs better third-down and early-down efficiency to stay on the field. He also said the travel was tiring and he was a little under the weather, but he feels fine now and is ready to play.

title: Shanahan Provides Injury Updates Ahead of Week 2 vs. Dolphins
headline: Kaelon Black is questionable for Week 2 and De'Zhaun Stribling is out; Upton Stout gets strong praise from Shanahan.
summary: Shanahan opened with injury news: De'Zhaun Stribling will be out for Week 2, while Dominick Puni and Kaelon Black are both listed as questionable. He described Black's status as only a "questionable amount of optimism" and did not say whether it is the same groin issue Black dealt with earlier. He also said the team may need to add a kicker from the practice squad, with two candidates still under consideration. On pre-snap motion, he said the team has always believed in it for angles and confusion, and that it takes many practice reps because the quarterback and motion man must match cadence, which gets harder on the road. He said the team's recovery from the Australia trip was uneven, with the first three or four days rough, but that players were fully recovered by Monday and Tuesday after an extra three days off. He defended the value of intense practice, arguing that the more teams practice football as it's played, the better prepared they are for Week 1. On the Dolphins, he called their offense explosive, especially their running back and quarterback, and warned that the defense can't let up. He praised Upton Stout's growth in year two, citing more knowledge of how opponents attack the nickel position. Overall, he framed the week around Black's uncertain status, the Stribling absence, and the Dolphins' playmakers.
